name: Wärtsilä Oyj Abp (Wärtsilä Corporation)
summary: Wärtsilä is a Finnish marine and energy technology group (founded 1834) supplying ship engines and propulsion, engine power plants for grid balancing, lifecycle services, and — through its Energy Storage & Optimisation business — utility-scale BESS (Quantum series) and the GEMS Digital Energy Platform. The storage business's ownership has moved in two stages: an 18-month strategic review concluded in March 2025 with retention (elevated to a standalone segment), but on 15 June 2026 Wärtsilä announced it will fold global Energy Storage into a 50/50 joint venture with Germany's RCT Solutions GmbH (RCT CEO Peter Fath to lead the JV; closing expected Q3 2026), reclassifying it as discontinued operations.
ecosystemRole: One of the established Western storage integrators: >19 GWh deployed or contracted across 130+ sites worldwide (company-reported), a global top-ten placement in Wood Mackenzie's inaugural BESS integrator ranking (July 2026), and an early leader in storage cybersecurity (first-in-industry IEC 62443 certification for GEMS technology). The 2025 numbers show the strategic squeeze: segment order intake fell 60% to EUR 455M (2,677 MWh, -52%) on US tariffs, FEOC rules, and price competition — the backdrop to the JV decision.

productsAndServices.name: Quantum3 BESS (September 2024)
productsAndServices.description: 5 MWh high-density AC block in a 20-ft ISO container with fully integrated batteries and string-based PCS, aluminum housing, back-to-back siting, US-engineered proprietary BMS, and low-GWP cooling — the flagship, powered by GEMS with rack-level control.

productsAndServices.name: Quantum2 BESS (March 2024)
productsAndServices.description: Pre-installed 4 MWh DC-block BESS in a CSC/ISO 20-ft enclosure for 2–8-hour applications, with IP67 liquid-cooled modules and configurable hybrid cooling.
highlights: Compliant with UL 9540A, NFPA 855, and IEC 62443-4 per its solution sheet

productsAndServices.name: GEMS Digital Energy Platform
productsAndServices.description: Energy-management software monitoring, controlling, and optimising storage and hybrid assets from cell to fleet level; the 7th generation (August 2024) adds autonomous, sub-second control of multi-GWh sites. Operated on 100+ projects across Australia, North America, Europe, Taiwan, and Chile.

productsAndServices.name: Engine power plants (Wärtsilä Energy)
productsAndServices.description: Flexible medium-speed engine plants balancing renewables — FY2025 Energy order intake EUR 2,940M (+31%) with 2,324 MW ordered (+69%), including Wärtsilä's first two US data-centre power projects totalling 789 MW.

productsAndServices.name: Services & marine (context)
productsAndServices.description: Group service net sales EUR 3,575M in 2025; Energy Storage service net sales EUR 23M (+52%) on the growing installed base. Marine (engines, propulsion, services) remains the group's largest segment at EUR 3,494M FY2025 net sales.

metrics.name: Storage JV impact
metrics.actual: Guided EUR -40 to -50M impact on 2026 operating result (write-downs/transformation costs); JV loss-making in 2026, positive results expected late 2027
metrics.result: Shares fell on both the March 2025 retention decision (>5%) and the June 2026 JV announcement; analysts cited weak profitability, 'very limited' engine–storage synergies, and no disclosed proceeds

periods.commentary: JV structure: 50/50 with RCT Solutions GmbH; consideration undisclosed; storage net assets <5% of Wärtsilä's total; ~480–588 personnel transfer; new investors may join later.
